stem: A hospital network's data center needs a connection to a VPC with bandwidth well beyond what a single internet-based tunnel can sustain, encryption for every byte in transit, and no leg of the path allowed to cross the public internet.

choices.text: Provision a standard AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection over the internet
Provision an AWS Direct Connect dedicated connection with no VPN
Create an AWS PrivateLink interface endpoint and connect the hospital's whole on-premises network to it directly
Provision a private Site-to-Site VPN over the Direct Connect connection through a transit gateway

rationale: Running a private-IP Site-to-Site VPN over a Direct Connect connection through a transit gateway supplies Direct Connect's dedicated, high-bandwidth private line while adding the IPsec encryption Direct Connect does not provide on its own, and none of the traffic crosses the public internet. A standard Site-to-Site VPN travels over the internet and is capped at a fraction of what a dedicated line delivers, failing the bandwidth and no-internet requirements. A Direct Connect connection with no VPN gives the private, high-bandwidth path but carries no encryption in transit, failing that requirement. PrivateLink publishes one specific service through an interface endpoint's elastic network interface; it has no mechanism to terminate an entire on-premises network's traffic, so it cannot stand in for a site-to-site connection.
